text:
Aisha: Heads up — optimize-toolkit regression alert just triggered in staging after quantization bump. p95 latency +12ms (~3%), throughput same. Rolling canary shows cache miss rate spiked. Ping owners @Jon @Priya :eyes:
Jon: looking now, do we have the eval that repros? link to logs
Aisha: yes — https://internal/ci/runs/4567 — stack shows KV cache TTL reset on model load after quantized weights applied
Priya: hmm that TTL reset was from the new model init path in pr #8342, assigned to me. I can revert the explicit `cache.invalidate()` but want to understand why it was added
Sam (eng-ml): it was added to avoid stale prefix cache across quant configs. We saw rare hallucinations in tests when cache had mixed dtype. But maybe we can scope invalidation to `model.version` instead
Theo: quick idea — set `cache.invalidate_on_model_change = false` and bump `cache.prefix_stability = true` for canary, see if p95 drops
Aisha: can we try that as a hotfix in canary first? Need a change by EOD
Jon: I'll open a small PR to toggle settings in the canary k8s config: `overrides/quant-canary.yaml` snippet:
```
cache:
  invalidate_on_model_change: false
  prefix_stability: true
```
PR: https://git/repo/pulls/902
Priya: also adding an eval run with the prompt set that caught the hallucination to make sure we don't regress
Sam (eng-ml): good — add `--seed=42` to keep runs deterministic
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary (canary-id: canary-552) — watching health
Jon: canary metrics after 5m: p95 down ~9ms, cache miss rate -40% :thumbsup:
Aisha: nice! Priya — if that looks safe, ship to dedicated tomorrow. Also please add a comment in #postmortems if we keep the invalidation change
Priya: will do. Opening follow-up ticket to audit other model-init invalidations
Ruth: adding ops to notify customers on Dedicated if we plan a wider rollout
Aisha: thanks everyone, closing loop — will update the rollout doc in the console repo
